blocks.text: Buying a Chicken Farm in BC: what the ground is and what governs it

items.t: Scope: broiler chicken farms anywhere in British Columbia — there is no neighbourhood, no MLS sub-area and no street boundary for this guide; the location facts for any real purchase are the farm's municipality and its Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status, checked parcel by parcel.
Identity: a buying-guide page, not a listing page and not an area page.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers

items.t: BOARD DISCIPLINE: Confirm each item with the BC Chicken Marketing Board directly before subjects are removed.
No unanswered FAQ question was spotted (all six structured questions carry answers) and there are no open-house listings on the page to conflict.

The address-check tool's coverage is narrower than the guide's scope: The guide is BC-wide, but its own ALR address-check tool covers Surrey, Langley (City and Township) and Abbotsford addresses per its text — a farm outside those municipalities gets no check from the tool and needs the ALC/local-government route directly.

faq.q: Is this a listings page for chicken farms?
faq.a: No: as read it is a buying guide — quota explainer, three routes into the industry, transfer process, cost decomposition and barn diligence — with no listing feed on the page itself; it links onward to the site's chicken-farms and poultry-farms listing pages.

faq.q: What should I check before buying a farm in This area?
faq.a: Check the ALR status, water source and licences, drainage and flood history, the buildings and any quota or production licences that do or do not transfer with the land. Poultry and egg production in BC are supply-managed, so a sale of the farm does not automatically include quota.

faq.q: What is the ALR and does it apply to farms in This area?
faq.a: The Agricultural Land Reserve is farmland protected by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission. Farm use is generally allowed on ALR land, but subdividing, adding homes or using the land for non-farm purposes usually needs approval, so check a property's ALR status before you offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in This area?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: What does a BC chicken farm cost?
faq.a: The page's "multi-million dollar range" framing is site copy only. A valuation stands on the specific land, barns, residence and any quota included, checked part by part.

faq.q: Can I split a farm parcel for a second homesite?
faq.a: Subdivision of ALR land generally requires ALC approval, and depositing a strata plan IS a subdivision (Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)) — a permission rule, not an absolute ban, but never assumed.
